title: Homeowner shares identified registration data
description: The homeowner registers an account on the Home Hub, which requires providing identified personal data such as credentials or contact information.

title: Linking via unique account identifier in transit
description: The data flow carries unique identifiers during account registration and device enrollment, enabling linking of the homeowner to specific cameras/sensors.

title: Processing of sensitive device enrollment data
description: The Home Hub receives and processes data about enrolled cameras and sensors, which can reveal sensitive details about the homeowner's property and activities.

title: Unawareness as user sharing personal data
description: The homeowner may not be fully aware of how their registration data and device enrollment information will be processed or stored by the Home Hub.

title: Linking via temporary access code
description: The temporary access code acts as a unique identifier that can link the guest's identity or actions to the door unlock event at the Home Hub.

title: Processing of identified access data
description: The Home Hub processes the temporary access code, which serves as identified information associating the specific guest with the access action.

title: Attributable access evidence
description: Receipt and potential logging of the access code at the Home Hub creates attributable evidence of the guest's action, preventing repudiation of the door unlock.

title: Profiling via stored sensor events
description: The local event log at DS1 stores motion/door/sensor events from the Home Hub, enabling pattern analysis to profile individuals' behavior and link events to specific data subjects.
assumptions: Events contain sufficient detail and volume for behavioral profiling over time.

title: Indefinite retention in event log
description: Personal sensor events are stored in the local log without specified limits, potentially keeping data longer than functionally necessary for the system's operation.
assumptions: No retention policy is enforced at the datastore level.
uncertainty_note: Flow description does not specify retention duration, so this is inferred from typical logging behavior.

title: Unawareness of event logging
description: Home Hub (P1) writes events without explicit indication that data subjects are made aware of the collection and storage of their motion/door/sensor activities.
assumptions: No user notification or consent mechanism described in the flow.

title: Sensitive video data uploaded
description: Home Hub uploads recorded camera clips which are highly sensitive personal data (home interior, individuals present) to cloud storage, exceeding minimal functional needs for basic recording.

title: Prolonged retention of clips
description: Cloud Video Storage receives and likely retains uploaded camera clips beyond the period functionally required for home monitoring purposes.

title: Revealing attributes in video clips
description: Uploaded camera clips contain visual attributes (faces, activities, home layout) that can reveal and identify data subjects.

title: Linking via upload metadata
description: The data flow may carry unique identifiers (device ID, account, timestamps) enabling linking of clips to specific users or households.

title: Unique identifier in motion alert metadata
description: The real-time motion alert flow likely includes a unique device or user identifier to route the notification correctly, allowing linking of the alert data to a specific individual across interactions.
assumptions: Alert payload or headers contain identifiers typical for such systems.

title: Identifier in forwarded alert
description: Home Hub shares motion alert containing unique reference (e.g. hub ID or account token) that identifies the data subject to the backend.
assumptions: Routing requires identification of the home/user.

title: Observed motion alert communications
description: Observation of the real-time data flow between Home Hub and backend can reveal the existence and timing of motion events in the home.
assumptions: Adversary can monitor network traffic to/from the hub.
uncertainty_note: Depends on encryption and network visibility; not asserted from description alone.

title: Propagation to backend service
description: Motion alert personal data is propagated to the mobile app backend, which may store or further process it beyond the immediate forwarding need.
assumptions: Backend may log or analyze alerts for additional purposes.

title: Unique identifier linking via push token
description: The push notification flow relies on a unique device token or identifier to deliver the motion-detected alert specifically to the homeowner's phone, linking the motion event data to that individual.

title: Identifier reference in notification delivery
description: The notification data flow includes or depends on a unique reference (device token) to the homeowner's identity to ensure delivery of the motion detection alert to the correct phone.

title: Detection via observed notification traffic
description: Observation of the push notification communication in transit can reveal the occurrence of motion events or system activity at the homeowner's location.

title: Analytics data shared with predetermined external party
description: The mobile app backend shares aggregated device-usage analytics with the cloud analytics vendor, making the data accessible to an external predetermined party beyond the core system.

title: Profiling groups from aggregated analytics
description: The cloud analytics vendor can use the received aggregated device-usage analytics to profile groups of individuals and transfer insights based on group membership or similarity.

title: Data subjects unaware of analytics sharing
description: End users of the mobile app are likely unaware that their device-usage data is aggregated and shared with an external cloud analytics vendor for processing.

title: Video contains revealing attributes enabling identification
description: The retrieved video clip includes visual attributes (e.g., faces, home environment) that support identification of the homeowner and other individuals present.

title: Video data serves as attributable evidence
description: The video clip record can be used to attribute actions or presence to individuals, preventing them from denying involvement in events captured.

title: Transfer of highly sensitive video data
description: The flow carries video clips which constitute sensitive personal data (surveillance footage from a private home) beyond minimal requirements for basic system operation.
